title: A Newborn Business: Esports
author: Zoltan Andrejkovics
target_audience: Business professionals and entrepreneurs interested in esports
Students and academics studying sports management, media, or technology
Investors and stakeholders evaluating new digital markets
core_themes: The rise and commercialization of competitive gaming
Structure and dynamics of the esports ecosystem
Roles of stakeholders: teams, players, organizers, brands, and media
Challenges and opportunities in an emerging industry
primary_purpose: To offer a detailed overview and analysis of the esports industry for readers new to the business side of competitive gaming, providing both big-picture context and specific, actionable insights.

structure_format.narrative_style: Informative, analytical, and accessible for non-experts
structure_format.organization: Sequential chapters covering the birth of esports, industry structure, major players, monetization, and future trends
features: Case studies from notable esports events
Breakdowns of business models and organizational roles

key_concepts_lessons: Esports has transitioned from grassroots gaming tournaments to a global, professionalized industry.
A complex network of stakeholders—including players, teams, sponsors, organizers, and publishers—forms the basis of current esports business.
Revenue streams include sponsorship, media rights, advertising, merchandising, and ticket sales, but the sustainability of these models is still evolving.
Branding, audience engagement, and effective event management are critical success factors.
Esports faces unique challenges such as regulation, athlete wellbeing, intellectual property issues, and questions of long-term profitability.
notable_features: Accessible entry point for readers without prior esports business knowledge
Analysis grounded in real-world case studies
Synthesizes industry data with strategic recommendations
cultural_historical_context: Published during a period (mid-2010s) of explosive global growth in competitive gaming, the book captures esports as it transforms from a niche hobby into a mainstream digital sport, highlighting both its opportunities and growing pains.
reception_impact: Recognized as an early and approachable guide to the business of esports
Valued for its structured, readable overview for entrepreneurs and newcomers
Used as supplementary material in sports management and media courses
Critiqued for less technical depth compared to more granular or academic esports analyses
comparable_titles: Esports Business Management by David Hedlund
Good Luck Have Fun: The Rise of Esports by Roland Li
This is Esports (and How to Spell it): An Insider’s Guide to the World of Pro Gaming by Paul Chaloner
